overview: Both give you a number, but digital PCR gets there by partitioning the sample so thoroughly that it can count molecules directly.
genZNote: One estimates quantity. One counts molecules one by one.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Quantifies template by tracking fluorescence in a single bulk reaction and comparing its Ct value to a standard curve.
aspects.valueB: Partitions a single sample into thousands of individual nano-scale reactions before amplification, then counts the fraction that are positive to calculate absolute concentration.

aspects.label: Quantification Approach
aspects.valueA: Relative to a standard curve — requires a calibration curve for absolute quantification.
aspects.valueB: Absolute quantification via Poisson statistics on the fraction of positive partitions — no standard curve required.

aspects.label: Reliance on Amplification Efficiency
aspects.valueA: Result accuracy depends heavily on consistent, well-characterized amplification efficiency across samples.
aspects.valueB: Endpoint-based counting of positive/negative partitions, making it far less sensitive to amplification efficiency variation.

aspects.label: Sensitivity for Rare Targets
aspects.valueA: Can struggle to detect a rare variant against a high background of wild-type template.
aspects.valueB: Well suited to detecting rare mutations or low-abundance targets against a high background, since each partition is scored independently.

aspects.label: Precision at Low Copy Number
aspects.valueA: Less precise at very low target concentrations.
aspects.valueB: Higher precision at low copy numbers, useful for minimal residual disease or low viral load monitoring.

aspects.label: Cost and Throughput
aspects.valueA: Lower cost per sample and higher throughput on standard instruments.
aspects.valueB: Higher cost per sample and generally lower throughput; specialized instrumentation is required.

aspects.label: Typical Research Applications
aspects.valueA: Routine gene expression analysis, standard pathogen load testing.
aspects.valueB: Rare mutation detection, copy number variation analysis, precise viral reservoir quantification.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Relative quantification via a standard curve.
aspects.valueB: Absolute quantification via partitioning and direct molecule counting.
